function: DDPG agents learn RSMA precoders and common-rate shares for max-min rate; AP selection uses PCA and an integer linear program, not learning (p. 5, 8).
system: Downlink cell-free MIMO RSMA: APs with 4 antennas, UEs with 2 (MISO variant with 1), 1.9 GHz, 20 MHz, no RIS (p. 3, 9).
method: DDPG actor-critic per AP, trained with federated averaging of weights at the CPU; pre-training, then fine-tuning by transfer learning after AP selection (p. 5, 7, 8).
data_channel: Custom simulator: Nakagami fading, piecewise path loss, 8 dB shadowing, random AP and UE positions in 1 km x 1 km, redrawn each training step (p. 3, 9).
test_conditions: Environment reset each training step; results for two cases (N,K)=(4,8) and (8,12) and sweeps of P_max, T^FL, N^UE; no train-test mismatch reported (p. 9).
baselines: Centralized DRL (same DDPG, at CPU), FDRL-RSMA-MISO, FDRL-SDMA-MIMO, and the convexified RSMA solution of [30], non-learned (p. 9).
metrics: Minimum UE rate (max-min rate, bit/s/Hz) versus P_max, episodes (convergence), T^FL and N^UE (p. 9, 10).
complexity: Order of complexity per training iteration of each NN: O(eta N^2 M'^2 (K^2 M'^2 + M^2 + K M M'^2)) (p. 9).
q1_support: p. 3: "Nakagami distribution"; custom simulator with a piecewise path loss, no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO, or measured data is used.
q2_support: p. 9: "Two cases for the number of APs and UEs have been considered"; each case is simulated separately (network size depends on N and K, p. 8) and the rest are sweeps of P_max, T^FL, N^UE; no unseen scenario.
q3_support: p. 9: "the centralized DRL-RSMA-MIMO, the FDRL-RSMA-MIMO, the FDRL-RSMA-MISO, as well as the FDRL-SDMA-MIMO"; non-learned baseline [30] exists, but the learned ones are centralized, MISO or SDMA variants of the proposed method, not an earlier learned method.
q4_support: p. 8: "computational complexity at each training iteration for each of the actor, target-actor, critic, and target-critic NNs is obtained" as an O(.) expression given on p. 9.
q5_support: p. 3: "Nakagami distribution"; channels are simulated and the paper gives no code or data link and uses no public channel dataset.
notes: The PDF is arXiv v1 (13 Jan 2025) and prints no DOI, so its identity with the DOI is not confirmable from the file. Federated aggregation is digital averaging at the CPU over fronthaul (p. 7), not over the air, so area 3 by function. The transfer-learning fine-tuning (p. 8) is a stage of the method, not a test in new conditions.
